<!-- pr-reviewer: be5d2ffcec46bb68ecb2e8f6e0d3b2c7c1082cd5 -->
## Review of #3489 (head `be5d2ffce`)

**Verdict: needs changes.** The workflow change is safe: no new trigger, scope or action. The watchdog is sound. But the report script has two inputs where a red main is reported as a runner stall. That is the dangerous direction. The two fixes are small.

## Workflow change

**A1. Triggers, runners, permissions.**
- The `on:` block is byte-identical to `origin/main`: `push: branches: [main]` and the existing `workflow_dispatch` with the input `ref`. There is no new trigger.
- `runs-on` of the two jobs is unchanged (`[self-hosted, camcraft-post-merge]`).
- The `permissions:` of each job are unchanged. The gate job keeps `contents: read`, `actions: read` and `pull-requests: read`. The report job keeps `contents: read` and `issues: write`.
- There is no new `uses:` action, no new secret, no changed checkout ref, and no new `continue-on-error`. The only `continue-on-error` is the existing one on `download-artifact`.
- New items: the job output `runner: ${{ runner.name }}` (the `runner` context is permitted in job outputs), `id: gate`, `timeout-minutes: 45`, and two `env:` values (`GATE_OUTCOME`, `RUNNER`). Both values go in through `env:`, not through `${{ }}` in a `run:` script.

**A2. The step timeout.**
- A step that hits `timeout-minutes` ends with a non-success outcome, and the job result is `failure`. The check `"$GATE_OUTCOME" != success` accepts each outcome that is not `success`, so it does not depend on the exact word.
- "Gate summary" and "Gate logs" have `always() && ...skip != 'true'`, so they run after a timeout. The logs upload and the summary line is written.
- If GitHub gives the job the result `cancelled` in place of `failure`, the report job does not run. Then nothing is reported. This is the safe direction (no false red), but the stall warning is lost.
- 45 minutes against a healthy run of about 21 minutes (27 minutes today, at most) is a margin of 18 minutes or more. That is safe.
- `gate-start.txt` is written at the start of the step, and the 44-minute check reads it in the next step. That is correct.

**A3. The report script: the four cases, and masking.**
- (a) A `FAIL` row in the summary, also beside `STALL` rows: red main, as before. Correct when the summary exists and is small (see blocker 2).
- (b) No `FAIL` row, but a `STALL` row or the timeout line: a warning, no `gh` call, exit 0. Correct.
- (c) Green: unchanged.
- (d) A red run with no summary and no timeout line: the script goes on to the old red path. Correct. An empty or missing `OUTPUT` file also goes to the red path (safe).
- The row match `^ +FAIL ` and `^ +STALL ` reads only the first word of a row (`row()` in `exec.rs`). A test name or a path cannot make a false row. CRLF is not a risk: the runner is Linux.
- Masking found: see blockers 1 and 2.

**A4. Shell injection.**
- Each value is double-quoted. There is no `eval`, and no `${{ }}` in a script body. Bash `echo` does not read backslash escapes.
- `$step` comes from the step names of the xtask plan (code in the repository) or from the gate's own `[NN] <name>` line. The test output goes to the step logs, not to stdout. The watchdog prints the last log lines to stdout with the prefix `     | `, so a test line cannot start a workflow command at the start of a line.
- `paste -sd ';'` makes `$step` one line. A `%0A` in a step name changes only the text of the warning, not the command.
- Result: no injection path. This is acceptable.

## Blockers

1. **`.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` line 112-118, and `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` line 40: the timeout path hides a FAIL that came before the hang.** The gate prints `     FAIL in <n>s <note>` when each step ends (`exec.rs` line 285), but the summary comes only at the end. Example: step 5 fails, and step 30 hangs at minute 25. The watchdog kills it at minute 40 at the earliest, so the 45-minute step timeout comes first. There is no summary, the timeout line is written, and the script reports a runner stall. The real FAIL opens no issue. With a normal run of 21-27 minutes and a watchdog of 15 minutes, a hang in the second half of the run always takes this path. Change: in "Gate summary", do not write the timeout line when `gate-output.txt` has a line that matches `^ +FAIL in `. Or, in the script, go to the red path when the output has such a line. Add a pinning case to `post_merge_stall.rs`: a progress `FAIL in` line, no summary, a timeout line: red main.
2. **`.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` line 36-37: `grep -q` with `pipefail` can hide a FAIL row.** The script has `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits at the first match. When the summary is larger than the pipe buffer (64 KiB on Linux), `printf` gets SIGPIPE and exits 141. Then the pipeline status is 141, `!` makes the condition true, and a run with FAIL and STALL rows is reported as a stall. Change: use `grep -E '^ +FAIL ' >/dev/null` (no `-q`), or `grep -qE '^ +FAIL ' <<<"$summary"`.

## Notes (no change needed for this PR)

- **A deadlock in the code looks like a stall.** A commit that makes a test hang gives a `STALL` row on each run. AGENTS.md **Runner stops** says "re-run it one time", but not what to do when the re-run stalls on the same step. Recommended: add one line: "A second `STALL` on the same step at the same commit is a red main: file it as such."
- **`watchdog::report` reads the log text, not the `End::Stalled` result.** A step log that has a line that starts with `error: gate watchdog: STALL ` (for example a failed test that prints such a log) changes a FAIL row to a STALL row. This is unlikely. A flag from `End::Stalled` through `direct::run` and `direct::cargo` is more robust. A follow-up is optional (`P7`).
- **The process kill (B6).** The tree is read by parent pid and killed by pid. Between the `ps` read and the `kill` there is a small pid-reuse window. A process that left the tree (a double fork, `setsid`) is not killed. A process group (Unix) or a job object (Windows) is safer. The gate itself is the parent and is not in the tree, so it lives and runs the other steps. In the capture path of `direct::cargo`, a surviving descendant that holds the stdout pipe keeps `reader.join()` blocked. The tree kill covers the normal case.
- **The stall times (B5).** Cargo prints a `Compiling <crate>` line on stderr for each crate when stderr is not a terminal, and libtest prints a line at the end of each test and at 60 s. 15 minutes for a debug step and 60 minutes of silence for a `--release` / `--ignored` step are sufficient. The silence of a heavy step is the longest single test or link, not the total of the heavy plan. `limit_for` reads the cargo args of the step, which contain `--release` and `--ignored` also for direct executables. Correct.
- **The exit code.** A STALL row has `ok == false`, so `bad` includes it. `exit_code(false, bad - stalled, stalled)` gives 1 for any FAIL, 3 for STALL rows only. A void run returns 1 before that line. `--failed` selects a stalled step again through the `error:` line. Correct.
- **Lanes.** The batch tier runs in parallel lanes. Then "last started step" in the timeout line is the last step that started, not always the step that hangs. The text is only a hint: acceptable.
- **B7, `known_fail.rs`.** `expect_fail_note` and `panic_block` moved without a change; `exec.rs` re-exports `expect_fail_note`. A pure move.
- **B7, the merge with #3470.** `git merge-tree` of `origin/main` (`893e749c0`) and this head is clean. `main.rs` on main moved `GateArgs` to `gate_args.rs`; this branch adds only three `mod` lines, in a different hunk. The only `Done { .. }` literals are in `exec.rs`, and the only callers of `direct::run` and `direct::cargo` are in `exec.rs`. Thus I expect the merged tree to compile. Not built.
- **B7, the `--covers` verdict.** On the merged tree, `heavy_covers::write` maps `d.ok` to the step result. A STALL row has `ok == false`, so it counts as failed, and the verdict is `FAIL`, never `PASS`. That is safe. The covers record prints the word `FAIL` for a stalled step, not `STALL`. A follow-up line is not necessary. It is optional (`P7`) if the record must name the stall.
- **`verdict::record`** also reads `d.ok`: a STALL is a failure there. Safe.
- **B8, the code shape.** No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new non-test code (`reader.join().unwrap_or_default()` is not a panic). `main.rs` has 410 lines and `exec.rs` has 377. `main.rs` is a little above the 400-line rule: acceptable for three `mod` lines.
- **B8, the tests.** `watchdog_tests.rs` has 7 `#[test]` functions (the `watchdog_helper` child included). They prove a silent tree is killed and named, that descendant output keeps a step alive, the parse of `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN`, the 4x factor, the row and exit code, and the walk of the tree. They ran on Windows only, so the Unix `ps` / `kill -KILL` path did not run. In `xtask/tests/post_merge_stall.rs`, the workflow-line test runs on each platform. The four script cases are `#[cfg(unix)]` and did not run on the author's machine (the author ran them by hand in Git Bash).
- **C, the rule text.** **Runner stops** agrees with the workflow: step timeout 45 minutes < "no output at 50 minutes" < job cap 90 minutes. The `gate` and `runners` skills and the decision file agree with the code. The body has `Process change: yes`, `Changelog: none` and `Fixes #3303`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

Built: not built by this review; the author's readings on this head: clippy clean, `cargo test -p xtask` green (282 unit tests and each integration binary); the Unix-only tests did not run.

Ready for a re-read: new head fac4e34ba. It fixes the two blockers and the three notes of the review of be5d2ffce. The PR body has the section "After the review". Clippy and `cargo test -p xtask` are green on fac4e34ba.

## Re-review of #3489 (head `fac4e34ba`, after the review of `be5d2ffce`)

**Verdict: ready.** The two blockers are closed. The three notes are done. I found no input where a real red main is reported as a stall or as green.

## Workflow change

- **Triggers, runners, permissions.** The diff of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` against `origin/main` changes no line of `on:`, `runs-on`, `permissions:`, `uses:`, secrets or `continue-on-error`. The change since the last review is only in the `run:` block of "Gate summary".
- **"Gate summary".** It writes the timeout line only when the gate step did not succeed, there is no `== gate summary` line, and there is no `^ +FAIL in ` line. Each `grep -q` reads a file directly, not a pipe. The new `|| true` on `grep ... | tail -n 1` stops `bash -e` when no `[NN]` line exists. It does not hide a real error: the pipe only reads a file, and a missing step line gives `none`.
- **The report script.** There is no `grep -q` in a pipe now (line 40 is a comment). Each grep reads a here-string or a file. `red_rows` is the `FAIL` rows of the summary. `red_progress` is each `^ +FAIL in ` line of the whole output. The stall path runs only when the two are empty. Without a summary, the issue body lists the `FAIL in` lines (`fails` falls back to `red_progress`), and the `tests/<name>.rs` extraction for the P1 check still works on these lines.
- **Shell injection.** Unchanged from the last review: each value is quoted, and there is no `eval` and no `${{ }}` in a script. The new `printf` uses a format string with `%s` only.

## The dangerous direction, with the new code

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `FAIL` rows only | red main |
| `STALL` rows only | runner stall (correct) |
| `FAIL` and `STALL` rows, also a summary of about 197 KB | red main (`a_large_summary_with_fail_and_stall_rows_stays_a_red_main`) |
| timeout line, no rows, no `FAIL in` | runner stall (correct) |
| a `FAIL in` line, then a hang and the timeout | red main; "Gate summary" writes no timeout line, and the script also checks `FAIL in` (`a_step_that_ended_red_before_a_timeout_stays_a_red_main`) |
| an empty or missing output file | red main, generic text |
| xtask does not build | red main, generic text (`a_red_run_with_no_summary_and_no_timeout_stays_red`) |
| the gate is cancelled by hand | the job result is `cancelled`; the report job does not run; nothing is reported, as on main. Not green |

- **False red.** `^ +FAIL in ` cannot match a test name or a log line. The gate prints step logs to stdout only in the STALL report, with the prefix `     | `. The word `FAIL in` comes only from the step-end line in `exec.rs`. A false red is not possible from the known output.
- **Two edge cases. Neither is a red main reported as a stall:**
  - A VOID run with `STALL` rows only reads as a stall. A VOID run has no verdict, so this is acceptable.
  - A deterministic hang that a commit causes reads as a stall on the first run. The new **Runner stops** line makes the second `STALL` of the same step at the same commit a red main.

## The notes of the last review

- **STALL from `End::Stalled`.** `direct::run` returns `(code, stalled)`, `direct::cargo` returns `(code, json, stalled)`, and `exec.rs` calls `watchdog::report` only when `stalled` is true. The log text no longer decides a STALL. `report` now reads the last watchdog line (`rposition`), and it has a fallback text when the line is missing (`a_stall_report_without_the_watchdog_line_still_names_the_step`). Done.
- **AGENTS.md "Runner stops".** It has the second-`STALL` line: "File it as a red main. Do not re-run it again." Done.
- **The decision file.** It names the parent-pid kill limits (the pid-reuse window, double fork, `setsid`, the held stdout pipe) and the follow-up #3493. Done.

## The merge with main (#3470)

- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main fac4e34ba` (main at `ce9d0d521`) is clean, with no conflicted file.
- On the merged tree, the only callers of `direct::run`, `direct::cargo` and `watchdog::report`, and the only `Done { .. }` literals, are in `exec.rs` and `watchdog_tests.rs`, from this branch. No file of main constructs `Done` or calls the changed functions. Thus I expect the merged tree to compile.
- The covers verdict: `heavy_covers::write` maps `d.ok`. A STALL step has `ok == false`, because `ok = ... && stall.is_none()` and `stall` is set from `End::Stalled`. Thus the verdict is `FAIL`, never `PASS`. This is still true.
- A compile check of the merged tree (`cargo check -p xtask --all-targets`) before the merge is recommended but not required, because the reading shows no shared caller. The coordinator says it runs one.

## Notes

- File sizes: `exec.rs` 380, `direct.rs` 233, `watchdog.rs` 165, `main.rs` 410. `main.rs` was 410 before; acceptable.
- `Process change: yes`, `Changelog: none` and `Fixes #3303` are in the body. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not edited.
- The Unix-only tests did not run: the four script cases and the two new ones in `xtask/tests/post_merge_stall.rs` (`#[cfg(unix)]`), and the `ps` / `kill -KILL` path. The author ran the six report cases and the summary block by hand under `bash -eo pipefail`. The first real run on the Linux runner is the first real check of these paths.

Built: not built by this review; the author's readings on this head: clippy clean, `cargo test -p xtask` green (283 unit tests and each integration binary, 0 failed); the Unix-only tests did not run.

Coordinator: this PR merges now.

- Class: no refresh. The PR merges cleanly with `main` (ce9d0d521).
- Review: comment 7081700251 on this exact head fac4e34ba (ready). It is also the independent read of the workflow change: the triggers, `runs-on`, the permissions, the actions and the secrets do not change.
- Gate: a local run of the trial merge with `main` ce9d0d521: `cargo check -p xtask --all-targets` passed; the `xtask` unit tests passed (289 passed, 0 failed; the 7 watchdog tests and the 5 `heavy_covers` tests are in that count); ten integration binaries passed; clippy is clean; `bash -n` and a YAML parse passed. The diff reaches no heavy lane.
- NOT run: the integration binary `catalog` on the trial merge (it builds the app CLI; it is not in this diff, and the author ran it on the head), and the six report-script tests of `post_merge_stall.rs`, which are Unix only. The author ran the same six cases by hand under `bash -eo pipefail`. The first post-merge run on a Linux runner is their first real check.
- Process change: the merging session makes the `PROCESS_VERSION` PR after this merge and comments on #681.
